column3: NASB puts the qualifying words in parentheses and adds “sent” and “the agency of.”
Close to the Greek. A full-width colon appears in the NASB text.
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text; it renders the phrase as “this present evil age.”
NASB renders “to the ages of the ages” as “forevermore.”
NASB renders “astonished” as “amazed” and “in the grace” as “by the grace.”
NASB adds “really” and renders “troubling” as “disturbing” and “pervert” as “distort.”
NASB renders “evangelize” as “preach … a gospel.”
NASB renders “evangelizing” as “preaching … a gospel.”
NASB follows the critical text without “for”; it renders “seek approval of” as “seeking the favor of,” adds “striving” and “trying,” and renders “servant” as “bond-servant.”
NASB follows the critical text (“For”); “I make known” is rendered “I would have you know.”
NASB adds “I received it.”
NASB renders “was destroying” as “tried to destroy” and adds “used to.”
NASB renders “more abundantly” as “more extremely” and “traditions of my fathers” as “ancestral traditions.”
NASB has “He” without “God,” following manuscripts that lack it; “having selected” is rendered “had set … apart.”
NASB renders “consulted” as “consult.”
NASB renders “the apostles before me” as “those who were apostles before me” and adds “once more.”
NASB follows the critical text (“Cephas”); “to make acquaintance” is rendered “to become acquainted.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB puts the verse in parentheses and renders “behold” as “I assure you.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB adds “still” and renders “by face” as “by sight.”
NASB puts the report in quotation marks; “were hearing” is rendered “kept hearing,” and “was destroying” is “tried to destroy.”
NASB renders “in me” as “because of me.”
